scenario.description: A facilities manager must approve the removal of an obsolete solvent storage tank so the bay can be prepared for a new dust-collection installation, and must finalize the isolation, waste handling, staging, and permit controls.

shared_context.S1: Solvent storage tank T-14 has been isolated from production for several months and occupies the expansion bay beside the finishing department.
shared_context.S2: The expansion bay is intended for installation of a new dust-collection system later this month.
shared_context.S3: Mara makes the binding facilities decision about whether and how T-14 is removed.
shared_context.S4: The plant's normal pre-work review brings maintenance, environmental, production planning, and permit compliance into the approval meeting before physical work is authorized; each specialist must formally enter their reviewed findings into the meeting record before Mara settles the work plan.

PF1.text: Jonas's maintenance assessment found that T-14 can be dismantled in exactly 6 labor hours and requires exactly 8 lockout points; he completed the field assessment yesterday but has not entered the work package into the maintenance system.

PF2.text: Priya's residue sample review classified the remaining tank residue as hazardous solvent waste requiring exactly 3 labeled drums and a signed waste-transfer manifest; the laboratory result arrived this morning and the environmental register has not yet been updated.

PF3.text: Caleb's floor-space review found that dismantled tank sections must be staged in marked area B12 because every other nearby staging area is reserved for the dust-collector installation; he confirmed the reservation with production scheduling this afternoon but has not circulated the updated bay map.

PF4.text: Nadia's permit review found that removing T-14 requires an internal hot-work and confined-space permit package, including a documented atmospheric test before cutting begins; she confirmed this against the current site permit matrix this week but has not attached it to the facilities request.

acceptance_conditions: T-14 must be decommissioned and removed.
The removal work package must specify exactly 6 labor hours.
The isolation plan must specify exactly 8 lockout points.
Exactly 3 labeled drums must be provided for the hazardous residue.
A signed waste-transfer manifest must be required.
Dismantled sections must be staged in area B12.
The internal permit package must be required.
An atmospheric test must occur before cutting begins.
The maintenance assessment must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The maintenance assessment changes the removal plan from an unspecified job to exactly 6 labor hours with exactly 8 lockout points, and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The hazardous classification changes waste handling from ordinary disposal to exactly 3 labeled drums and a required signed waste-transfer manifest.
The production-space reservation changes the staging assignment from an unspecified nearby area to exactly area B12.
The permit review changes the work controls from a routine removal approval to a required permit package with an atmospheric test before cutting.
